transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-14
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Aiden Cross (TitaniumGrid Head of Partnerships), Nora Kim (TitaniumGrid Solutions Architect), Diego Ramos (TitaniumGrid Sales Director)

Auto-summary: quick partner intro; discuss where TitaniumGrid's managed GPU offering could fit into Redwood's Dedicated / Private models; agree to run a benchmark and share security docs.

[00:00] Jordan: All right, hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE — and with me is Maya our solutions engineer. How's it going at TitaniumGrid?

[00:07] Aiden: Hey Jordan thanks, good. I'm Aiden, head of partnerships. We've been wanting to explore tighter integrations with inference platforms; we run managed GPU clusters across multi-tenant and dedicated racks.

[00:15] Nora: Hi, Nora here — I'm the solutions architect. We're particularly curious about how Redwood routes requests and the Dedicated capacity model, like, how isolation works and what we can co-sell.

[00:24] Maya: Awesome, thanks. Quick agenda: intro partner programs, high level Redwood infra (hosted/dedicated/private), security/compliance, and then discuss a bench / POC path. Sound good?

[00:33] Diego: Yep, that's perfect.

[00:36] Jordan: Cool. Very quick from our side — Redwood is a dev-first inference platform, we provide hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity that can be run on partner hardware or our fleets, and Private deployments for VPC/on-prem customers. The differentiator is we optimize for production economics: predictable latency, cost controls, batching, KV cache, etc.

[00:55] Aiden: When you say "run on partner hardware," do you mean a full private deployment into our datacenter, or more like a dedicated tenancy in our cloud?

[01:05] Maya: Both. We do a few patterns — 1) we can run a private control plane in your VPC (customer-managed), 2) we can provision Dedicated capacity that lives on partner-hosted GPU pools and gets routed for a customer (we can do peering), or 3) full on-prem with an air-gapped option for regulated customers.

[01:21] Nora: For our customers, the big asks are SSO/SAML, KMS integration, and audit logs. They also ask about SOC2. Do you have SOC2?

[01:30] Jordan: Yes, Redwood is SOC 2 Type II. We'll share the whitepaper and security packet after this call — I'll drop a link (see next steps).

[01:36] Diego: On the infra side, our racks are A100 and H100 mixes; we also have custom cooling and NVLink fabrics. How sensitive is Redwood to the exact GPU topology?

[01:46] Maya: Great question. It depends on the model and the sequence length; our kernel selection and compilation layer will pick optimized kernels for the target hardware. For large models H100s obviously give better perf, but we also support quantized pipelines for A100s. We can tune batch sizes and the runtime chooses KV cache strategies — though sometimes the transcriber (laughs) — the notes say K-V cash — anyway — that stuff matters for warm starts.

[02:10] Aiden: Ha — K-V cash — noted. We're seeing a lot of customers who care about latency tail. What's your typical P95 for a 2k token generation on Dedicated?

[02:18] Maya: It's workload dependent — but small-ish models we see sub-150ms token latencies at steady state; for large LLMs with longer generations it increases. Important lever is batching vs single-request latency. We can show benchmark numbers — I'll share the sample results.

[02:33] Nora: We also have an orchestration layer that prefers affinity packing; would Redwood allow us to expose metrics or tie into your tracing?

[02:41] Jordan: Yes, Redwood Console has tracing hooks and per-route dashboards. For partner-deployed Dedicated, we can surface token-level cost and latency metrics to your ops team via a secure dashboard or push logs into your workspace.

[02:53] Aiden: What about network? If we're hosting Dedicated nodes, do you require a public endpoint or can we do private peering?

[03:00] Maya: Private peering is supported. We typically recommend VPC peering or private link. For certain enterprise customers we run a private control plane in their VPC so all traffic stays internal.

[03:09] Diego: Commercially, are you looking for reseller partnerships or more of a technology integration?

[03:14] Jordan: Both are possible. We have a partner program that supports reseller and co-sell motions, revenue share, and technical integrations. We'll send the partner doc that outlines tiers.

[03:23] Aiden: Cool. Can we talk briefly about a pilot? Ideally we'd like a benchmark with one of our standard models — say a 7B/13B mix — and see how Redwood's runtime behaves on our H100 hosts under mixed load.

[03:35] Maya: Totally. Proposed POC: we run a 2-week bench — Redwood SE + TitaniumGrid infra — use your models or ours, run throughput and latency tests, plus run KV-cache warm path tests. I'll provide the benchmark script. We'll need workload samples and token distribution from you.

[03:52] Nora: We'll prepare those. Also, re: security — our customers sometimes require KMS integration for customer-managed keys. Is that supported?

[03:59] Jordan: Yes, we integrate with KMS/HSM providers. For private deployments you can bring your own keys. We'll include the KMS integration guide in the doc packet.

[04:10] Diego: Any blockers around multitenancy? Our offering supports both multi-tenant managed and dedicated single-tenant. For Redwood Dedicated, do you isolate KV caches per customer?

[04:19] Maya: Yes, isolation is per-tenant. KV cache and prefix caching are scoped; for Dedicated we can pin capacity and ensure data isolation. There are also routing policies — e.g., route low-cost requests to A100 quantized variants, and latency-critical to H100 instances for a tiered offering.

[04:34] Aiden: Let's talk errors and fallbacks. If capacity in a region is constrained, do you auto-fallback to another model variant or region?

[04:42] Jordan: We have smart routing — requests can be routed by policy (latency, cost, region) and we can automatically fallback to compatible model variants or regionally adjacent pools to keep apps online. That is part of Redwood's reliability play.

[04:55] Nora: For the bench, can we instrument network latency from our edge to your control plane? We want to quantify end-to-end latency.

[05:03] Maya: Yep, we'll include network probes as part of the script. We'll want to coordinate times so you can enable any necessary firewall rules for the peering.

[05:12] Diego: On commercial terms — for Dedicated on partner hardware, do you have a revenue share?

[05:17] Jordan: We do partner revenue share models; it depends on scale and commitment. We'll include sample economics in the partner deck and then follow up with legal.

[05:25] Aiden: Cool. One question: Is Redwood open to co-marketing for large deployments?

[05:29] Jordan: Yes, co-marketing and case studies are part of higher-tier partnerships. Happy to discuss specifics if there's mutual customer interest.

[05:36] Nora: Any compliance/regulatory constraints? Some of our customers in finance ask about data residency. Can we pin data to region?

[05:43] Maya: Data residency is supported — you can pin capacity to specific regions and we can run private control planes in those regions to satisfy residency.

[05:50] Aiden: Great. Let's go through planned next steps so we're aligned.

[05:53] Jordan: Ok recap: Jordan will send partner deck + pricing + SOC2 and security packet. Maya will share benchmark script and an infra checklist. TitaniumGrid will provide workload samples and token distribution, and we schedule a bench in the next 10 business days. Anything else?

[06:12] Diego: We'll also need a rough NDA for the benchmark? We prefer one to protect customer examples.

[06:18] Jordan: We can do an NDA — I'll attach the standard partner NDA in the follow-up email.

[06:22] Nora: One last technical: are there any drivers or kernel versions you require on the hosts for optimum perf?

[06:27] Maya: Generally recent CUDA + cuDNN and the NVIDIA drivers for H100/A100 — we'll document exact versions. For NVLink specifics we'll call out recommended configs.

[06:36] Aiden: Perfect. Sounds like we're aligned.

[06:39] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and proposed bench schedule.

[06:45] Aiden: Thanks, appreciate it.

[06:47] Diego: Thanks all.

[06:49] Jordan: Bye.

[06:52] (end)
